block.description: The stdlib provider provides additional custom functions for use within Terraform's HCL2 configuration language.

id.description: Aliased to string input parameter(s) for efficiency and proper plan diff detection.

list_one.description: First input list parameter to compare with the second.

list_two.description: Second input list parameter to compare with the first.

result.description: Function result storing whether the two maps are equal.

block.description: Returns a comparison between two lists. The elements are compared sequentially, starting at index 0, until one element is not equal to the other. The result of comparing the first non-matching elements is returned. If both lists are equal until one of them ends, then the shorter list is considered less than the longer one. The result is 0 if list_one == list_two, -1 if list_one < list_two, and +1 if list_one > list_two. The input lists must be single-level.

after.description: Function result storing the input string after the separator.

before.description: Function result storing the input string before the separator.

block.description: Returns the strings before and after the first instance of the separator in the input string. Also returns whether or not the separator was found in the input string. If the separator is not found in the input string, then `found` will be false, `before` will be equal to `param`, and `after` will be an empty string.

coalesce_map.description: Takes any number of map arguments and returns the first one that is not empty.
coalesce_map.summary: Empty coalesce one or more maps

variadic_parameter.name: map
variadic_parameter.description: One or more of the input maps to coalesce.

combinations.description: Return the number of combinations given a set with a number of elements, and a selection size.

parameters.name: num_elements
parameters.description: Input number parameter for the number of elements in a set from which to make a selection. This value cannot be negative since the resultant 'NaN' is not allowed in Terraform types.

parameters.name: selection_size
parameters.description: Input number parameter for the number of elements to select from the set. This value cannot be negative since the resultant 'NaN' is not allowed in Terraform types.

compact_map.description: Return a map with all of the key-value pairs removed where the corresponding value is `null` or an empty String.

parameters.name: map
parameters.description: Input map to compact.

compare_list.description: Returns a comparison between two lists. The elements are compared sequentially, starting at index 0, until one element is not equal to the other. The result of comparing the first non-matching elements is returned. If both lists are equal until one of them ends, then the shorter list is considered less than the longer one. The result is 0 if list_one == list_two, -1 if list_one < list_two, and +1 if list_one > list_two. The input lists must be single-level.
compare_list.summary: Compare the elements of two lists similar to the spaceship operator

parameters.name: list_one
parameters.description: First input list parameter to compare with the second.

parameters.name: list_two
parameters.description: Second input list parameter to compare with the first.

compare_string.description: Lexicographically compares two strings and returns an integer indicating their relationship. A `-1` indicates the first string is lexicographically less than the second string, `0` indicates they are equal, and a `1` indicates the first string is lexicographically greater than the second string.
compare_string.summary: Compare two strings similar to the spaceship operator.

parameters.name: string_one
parameters.description: First input string parameter to compare with the second.

parameters.name: string_two
parameters.description: Second input string parameter to compare with the first.

count.description: Return the number of non-overlapping instances of a substring in a string. The substring cannot be empty as this counts the number of Unicode code points in the string (before and after each rune), and this is awkward within Terraform.
count.summary: Counts the number of non-overlapping instances of a substring in a string.

parameters.name: string
parameters.description: Input string parameter for determining the number of occurrences of the substrings within it.

parameters.name: substring
parameters.description: Input substring parameter for determining the number of occurrences of that substring in a string.

cut.description: Returns the strings before and after the first instance of the separator in the input string. Also returns whether or not the separator was found in the input string. The return is a tuple: `before`, `after`, `found`. If the separator is not found in the input string, then `found` will be false, `before` will be equal to the `string` parameter, and `after` will be an empty string.

parameters.name: string
parameters.description: Input string parameter for cutting around a separator.

parameters.name: separator
parameters.description: The separator for cutting the input string.

elements_delete.description: Return the list where values are deleted beginning and ending inclusively at two specific element indices. This function errors if the `end_index` is out of range for the original list (greater than or equal to the length of the `list` parameter).

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: Input list parameter for which the values will be deleted.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Index in the list at which to begin deleting the values (inclusive).

parameters.name: end_index

empty.description: Return whether the input parameter of one of four possible different types (String, Set, List, or Map) is empty or not. Other types will error due to lack of definition for emptiness.

parameters.name: values

variadic_parameter.name: all
variadic_parameter.description: Optional: Whether to check for all of the values instead of the default any of the values.

last_char.description: Return the last character(s) of an input string parameter. Only the terminating character is returned by default unless a value for `num_chars` is defined.

parameters.description: Input string parameter for determining the last character.

variadic_parameter.name: number_of_characters
variadic_parameter.description: Optional: The number of terminating characters at the end of the string to return (default: 1). This must be less than or equal to the number of characters in the input string.

last_element.description: Return one or more terminating element(s) of an input list parameter.
last_element.summary: Return the last element of a list

parameters.name: list

variadic_parameter.name: number_of_elements
variadic_parameter.description: Optional: The number of terminating elements at the end of the list to return (default: 1). This can be thought of as functionally analogous to a 'reverse slice'.

parameters.description: Input string parameter for searching for the substring.

parameters.name: substring

list_index.description: Return the index of the first occurrence of the element parameter in the list parameter, or return `-1` if the element parameter is not present in the input list parameter.
list_index.summary: Return index of element in list

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: Input list parameter for determining the element's index.

parameters.name: element
parameters.description: Element in the list to determine its index.

variadic_parameter.name: sorted
variadic_parameter.description: Optional: Whether the list is sorted in ascending order or not (note: see `stdlib::sort_list`). If the list is sorted then the efficient binary search algorithm will be utilized, but the combination of sorting and searching may also be less efficient overall in some situations.

parameters.description: Input list parameter for determining the maximum number.

max_string.description: Return the maximum string (last by lexical ordering) from the elements of an input list parameter.

product.description: Return the product of the elements within a set. This is similar to the core `sum` function, but for a mathematical product instead.
product.summary: Return the product of a set's elements.

parameters.name: set
parameters.description: Input set parameter for determining the product. The set must contain at least one element.

repeat.description: Return a list or string that repeats the input list or string the specified number of times.
repeat.summary: Return a repeated list or string.

parameters.name: repeater
parameters.description: Input list or string parameter for repeating. The list or string must contain at least one element.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of times to repeat the input list or string. This cannot be a negative number.

replace.description: Return the list where values are replaced at a specific element index (inclusive). This function errors if the `end_index`, or the specified `index` plus the length of the `replace_values` list, is out of range for the original list (greater than or equal to the length of the `list` parameter).

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: Input list parameter for which the values will be replaced.

parameters.name: replace_values
parameters.description: Input list of values which will replace values in the list.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: Index in the list at which to begin replacing the values (inclusive).

variadic_parameter.name: end_index
variadic_parameter.description: Optional: The index in the list at which to finish replacing values (inclusive). If the difference between this and the `index` is greater than or equal to the length of the list of the `replace_values`, then the additional elements in the original `list` will all be zeroed (i.e. removed; see third example of `provider::stdlib::replace`). This parameter input value is only necessary for that situation as otherwise its value will be automatically deduced by the provider function.

round.description: Return the nearest integer of an input parameter; rounding half away from zero.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Input number parameter for determining the rounding.

variadic_parameter.name: even
variadic_parameter.description: If true then round 'ties' (i.e. `.5`) to the nearest even integer instead. Specifying `false` is the same as not providing an input value for this parameter (default behavior).

sort_list_number.description: Return the list where numeric values are sorted in ascending order.
sort_list_number.summary: Sort the numeric elements in a list

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: Input list parameter for sorting. This must be at least size 2.

sort_list_string.description: Return the list where string values are sorted in ascending order. Note that the Terraform 'types' package has issues converting some numbers for comparisons such that e.g. 49 will be sorted before 5 due to 4 < 5, but 45 would be correctly sorted before 49. Therefore, it would be preferred to use `sort_list_number` for lists of numbers not implicitly cast or recast to strings.
sort_list_string.summary: Sort the string elements in a list

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: Input list parameter for sorting. This must be at least size 2.

split_after.description: Return a list of strings by splitting an input string parameter after each occurrence of a separator. If the separator is not empty nor present within the string, then the return value will be a list containing the original string as the only element instead. This function is roughly equivalent to the `split` function in Terraform core, but additionally retains the separator as part of the returned list elements.
split_after.summary: Produces a list by splitting a given string after each occurrence of a separator.

parameters.name: string
parameters.description: Input string parameter for searching for the substring.

parameters.name: separator
parameters.description: Input separator parameter for searching within the string.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Input number parameter for determining the square root. This number cannot be negative, infinite (positive or negative), or NaN.

truncate.description: Return the integer value of an input parameter.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Input number parameter for determining the truncated integer value.
